title: Animals
description: Animals have life cycles, behaviours, and adaptations. Pollinators and seed dispersers help plants reproduce. Group behaviour provides survival benefits.

exercises.question: A RUBY-THROATED HUMMINGBIRD is a pollinator. What does it do for plants?
choices: it transfers pollen between flowers while drinking nectar
it provides shade for young plants
exercises.exp: Hummingbirds hover at flowers to drink nectar. Pollen sticks to them and transfers to the next flower — pollination!

exercises.question: An INDIAN FLYING FOX (fruit bat) is a pollinator. It pollinates mostly ___.
exercises.exp: Flying foxes are nocturnal — they pollinate night-blooming plants while searching for fruit and nectar.

exercises.question: A PAINTED LADY BUTTERFLY pollinates flowers. Which body part picks up pollen?
choices: its legs and body as it lands on flowers
exercises.exp: As a butterfly lands on a flower to sip nectar, pollen sticks to its fuzzy legs and body — then transfers to the next flower!

exercises.question: A EURASIAN RED SQUIRREL disperses seeds by ___.
choices: burying nuts and acorns and forgetting some — which then grow into new plants
exercises.exp: Squirrels bury nuts for winter but forget many — those nuts sprout into new trees! Great seed dispersal.

exercises.question: An AFRICAN ELEPHANT disperses seeds by ___.
choices: eating fruit and depositing seeds far away in its dung
swimming and dropping seeds in water
exercises.exp: Elephants travel huge distances, eating fruit and leaving seeds in their dung far from where the fruit grew!

exercises.question: A COMMON OSTRICH disperses seeds by ___.
choices: eating fruit and depositing seeds in droppings as it walks across large areas
exercises.exp: Ostriches eat fruit and walk great distances — seeds pass through and are deposited in new areas in their droppings.

exercises.question: Why do NORTH AMERICAN CARIBOU travel in large herds of thousands?
choices: for warmth, safety from predators, and easier navigation during migration
they compete with each other for food
exercises.exp: Massive caribou herds confuse predators, share warmth, and help individuals navigate — safety in numbers!

exercises.question: AFRICAN WILD DOGS hunt cooperatively in a pack. The MAIN benefit is ___.
choices: they can sleep while one dog hunts
they can bring down prey much larger than one dog could alone
exercises.exp: Pack hunting lets wild dogs take down large antelopes — prey impossible for a single dog to catch alone.

exercises.question: LEAFCUTTER ANTS carry leaf pieces back to their colony. What do they use them for?
choices: to grow fungus inside the colony which they then eat
exercises.exp: Leafcutter ants do not eat the leaves — they grow a special fungus on them underground, and eat the fungus!

exercises.question: What benefit does GROUP BEHAVIOUR provide for most social animals?
choices: protection from predators, shared food finding, and warmth
they compete more with each other
exercises.exp: Living in groups helps animals defend against predators (more eyes), find food, stay warm, and care for young.

exercises.question: Which is an example of POLLINATION?
choices: a bird eating berries and moving the seeds elsewhere
a bee collecting nectar and brushing pollen from one flower to another
exercises.exp: Pollination moves pollen from one flower's anther to another flower's stigma — enabling seed formation.

exercises.question: Without POLLINATORS, what would happen to many flowering plants?
choices: they could not reproduce and would eventually die out
nothing — plants do not need pollinators
exercises.exp: Most flowering plants depend on pollinators (bees, butterflies, birds) to transfer pollen so they can make seeds!

exercises.question: A HONEY BEE collects nectar and pollen. Pollen sticks to tiny hairs on the bee's body. What happens next?
choices: the bee eats the pollen and digests it completely
the bee carries pollen to the next flower, transferring it to the stigma — pollinating the plant
the bee buries the pollen underground
the pollen washes off in the rain immediately
exercises.exp: Pollen on the bee's body rubs off onto the next flower's stigma — pollinating it. The bee gets nectar; the plant gets pollinated. Mutual benefit!

exercises.question: MIGRATORY MONARCH BUTTERFLIES travel up to 4,500 km from Canada to Mexico. What is the KEY reason for this migration?
choices: they travel to lay eggs in Canada
they migrate south in autumn to overwinter in warm Mexican forests where they survive the cold season
they travel to find flowers in Mexico
exercises.exp: Monarchs cannot survive Canadian winters — they migrate to mountain forests in Mexico where millions cluster together to survive, then return north in spring.

exercises.question: SEED-EATING BIRDS (like finches) have short, strong, CONE-SHAPED BEAKS. Why?
choices: to crack open hard seed shells — the shape provides mechanical advantage for splitting seeds
exercises.exp: A short, conical beak works like nutcrackers — concentrating force to crack hard seed shells. Beak shape is adapted to diet!

exercises.question: EMPEROR PENGUINS huddle together in groups of thousands during Antarctic winters. Why?
choices: to conserve body heat — the group reduces each individual's heat loss in -60°C winds
exercises.exp: Huddling reduces the surface area exposed to freezing Antarctic winds — individuals in the centre lose much less heat than those at the edge. They take turns at the outside!

exercises.question: WOLVES howl to communicate. What information can a howl convey?
choices: only that the wolf is hungry
territory boundaries, location, rallying the pack, and bonding — howls carry many messages
exercises.exp: Wolf howls are complex — they can signal territory (warning other packs), rally scattered pack members, coordinate hunts, and strengthen social bonds.

exercises.question: A CLEANER FISH removes parasites from a larger fish's body. The larger fish does not eat the cleaner fish. This is an example of ___.
exercises.exp: Mutualism: both benefit! The cleaner fish gets food (parasites); the larger fish gets cleaned. This is a classic cleaning station relationship!

exercises.question: BEARS eat fish, berries, honey, and insects. This makes them ___.
choices: omnivores — they eat both plant and animal matter
exercises.exp: Omnivores eat both plants and animals. Bears are perfect omnivores — adapting their diet to whatever is available seasonally.

exercises.question: CANADA GEESE fly in a V-FORMATION during migration. The bird at the FRONT works hardest. Why do birds rotate the lead position?
choices: to take turns being in charge
to share the hardest work — the lead bird fights most air resistance; rotating prevents exhaustion
exercises.exp: The lead bird creates turbulence but gets no lift benefit. Birds behind exploit updrafts from the leader's wings. They rotate so no single bird exhausts itself!

exercises.question: BARN OWLS hunt in complete DARKNESS. What special adaptation do they use?
choices: they have very large eyes that see UV light
asymmetrically placed ears that detect the exact direction of sound with incredible precision, allowing them to hunt by hearing alone
exercises.exp: Barn owls have asymmetric ear placement — one higher than the other. This lets them pinpoint sounds in 3D with extraordinary accuracy — hunting by sound alone in the dark!

exercises.question: Why is BIODIVERSITY important in an animal community?
choices: more species means more competition and less food
greater biodiversity makes the community more stable and resilient — if one species declines, others can fill its role
only one species is needed in each community
exercises.exp: Diverse communities have more interconnected food webs — if one species is lost, others can partially replace its role. Biodiversity = stability and resilience!

exercises.question: BATS use ECHOLOCATION to hunt insects at night. What is echolocation?
choices: emitting high-pitched sound pulses and listening to the echoes to determine prey location and distance
using eyes to see in the dark
exercises.exp: Bats emit ultrasonic chirps (too high for humans to hear) and listen to the echo bouncing back — calculating distance, size, and speed of prey!

exercises.question: A HERMIT CRAB lives in an empty shell made by another animal. This is an example of ___.
choices: commensalism — the crab benefits; the shell's maker is unaffected
exercises.exp: Commensalism: one organism benefits (hermit crab gets a home), the other is neither helped nor harmed (the dead snail's shell sits unused otherwise).

exercises.question: SALMON swim upstream to spawn (lay eggs). After spawning, adult salmon die. How does this benefit the ecosystem?
choices: their decaying bodies provide nutrients that fertilise riverside forests and feed other animals
exercises.exp: Salmon carry ocean nutrients inland — their bodies feed bears, eagles, and insects, and fertilise riverside trees. Dead salmon are recycled nutrients!

exercises.question: ANIMALS that are NOCTURNAL are active at night. What adaptations help them?
choices: bright colour vision for spotting predators
large pupils for collecting more light, sensitive hearing, and sometimes echolocation or heat sensing
thick fur for protection from daylight
they sleep during predator activity times
exercises.exp: Nocturnal animals have large, light-gathering eyes (cats, owls) and/or other senses (hearing, smell, echolocation) that work in darkness.

exercises.question: AFRICAN CAPE BUFFALO live in herds and will charge at predators together to protect sick members. This behaviour is ___.
choices: cooperative group defence — individuals work together to protect the whole herd
exercises.exp: Cape buffalo cooperate to defend herd members — they will even rescue captured individuals from lions! Group defence is much more effective than individual defence.

exercises.question: CLOWNFISH live among the STINGING TENTACLES of sea anemones (which kill other fish). The anemone does not sting the clownfish. This relationship is ___.
choices: parasitism — the anemone hurts the clownfish
mutualism — the clownfish chases away butterflyfish that eat anemones; the anemone provides protection to the clownfish
exercises.exp: Classic mutualism! The clownfish drives away anemone predators and eats parasites; the anemone provides protection. Both organisms benefit!

exercises.question: HIBERNATING ANIMALS survive winter by ___.
choices: entering a deep sleep, lowering body temperature and metabolism to conserve energy when food is scarce
exercises.exp: Hibernation dramatically slows metabolism — heart rate drops from 50+ to just 8 beats/min in bears. They survive on stored fat without eating for months!

exercises.question: Why do CUCKOOS lay their eggs in OTHER BIRDS' nests?
choices: cuckoos are brood parasites — tricking other birds into raising their chicks, saving the cuckoo energy for reproduction
they are protecting other birds' eggs
cuckoos have no eggs of their own
exercises.exp: Brood parasitism: the cuckoo lays its egg in another bird's nest. The host bird raises the cuckoo chick (which often pushes other eggs out). Clever but cruel!

exercises.question: Animals that migrate often use a COMBINATION of navigation tools. Which combination do monarch butterflies use?
choices: the sun's position as a compass + sensing Earth's magnetic field
smell trails left by previous generations
exercises.exp: Monarchs use a sun compass (adjusted for time of day using internal clocks) and Earth's magnetic field — a built-in GPS without technology!

exercises.question: A butterfly's life cycle goes: egg → larva (caterpillar) → pupa (chrysalis) → adult. This is called ___.
choices: complete metamorphosis — four distinct stages with dramatic changes
a life cycle with no metamorphosis
exercises.exp: Complete metamorphosis has 4 stages: egg → larva → pupa → adult. The pupa stage is where dramatic internal reorganisation happens!

exercises.question: Which type of animal has a THREE-CHAMBERED HEART (most have two ventricles and one atrium)?
exercises.exp: Most reptiles and amphibians have 3-chambered hearts. Fish have 2, birds and mammals have 4. The 4-chambered heart is most efficient for warm-blooded activity!

exercises.question: An ENDOTHERM (warm-blooded animal) maintains its body temperature by ___.
choices: internal metabolic processes — burning food to generate body heat regardless of environment
exercises.exp: Endotherms (mammals, birds) generate heat internally through metabolism. This allows activity in cold environments — a huge survival advantage over ectotherms!

exercises.question: A REPTILE on a cold morning is SLUGGISH. Why?
choices: reptiles are ectotherms — their body temperature matches the environment; cold = slow metabolism = sluggish movement
their muscles work better in cold air
exercises.exp: Ectotherms (reptiles, fish, amphibians) rely on external heat. Cold morning = cold body = slow muscle contractions = sluggish. Warm up first, then they become active!

exercises.question: Why do DEEP-SEA FISH glow in the dark (bioluminescence)?
choices: they absorb sunlight at the surface and release it when deep
chemicals (luciferin + oxygen) react to produce light — used for attracting prey, mates, or confusing predators
they reflect light from volcanic vents
all animals glow but we cannot see it near the surface
exercises.exp: Bioluminescence is chemical light production — no heat! Anglerfish use it to lure prey in total darkness. Some squid use it to confuse predators.

exercises.question: What is the main purpose of FEATHERS on a bird?
choices: flight (in flying birds), insulation (warmth), waterproofing, and communication — multiple functions
only to make birds look beautiful
exercises.exp: Feathers are multifunctional: flight feathers provide lift, down feathers insulate, oil-coated feathers waterproof. Birds signal with colourful feathers!

exercises.question: Which of these animals is a MARSUPIAL?
choices: a kangaroo — marsupials raise young in a pouch
exercises.exp: Marsupials are mammals whose young are born at an early developmental stage and complete development in a pouch. Kangaroos, koalas, and wombats are marsupials!

exercises.question: A SYMBIOTIC RELATIONSHIP where both species BENEFIT is called ___.
exercises.exp: Mutualism: both benefit. Clownfish protect anemones from predators; anemones protect clownfish with stinging tentacles. Bees and flowers also share mutualism!

exercises.question: PARASITISM is a relationship where ___.
choices: one organism (parasite) benefits at the EXPENSE of the other (host)
one benefits, the other is unaffected
exercises.exp: Parasites exploit hosts for food/shelter, often harming them. Ticks, tapeworms, and mistletoe plants are parasites. Host survives but is weakened.

exercises.question: ECHOLOCATION allows bats and dolphins to navigate by ___.
choices: seeing very far in the dark
emitting high-pitched sounds and listening to the echoes to create a 'sound picture' of the environment
detecting magnetic fields and electric fields
exercises.exp: Echolocation: animals send out pulses of sound and analyse returning echoes to detect objects with precision. Bats can detect a moth-sized object in total darkness!

exercises.question: A KEYSTONE SPECIES has a disproportionately large effect on its ecosystem. Which would cause the most damage if removed?
choices: sea otters — removing them causes sea urchin populations to explode, destroying kelp forests
exercises.exp: Without sea otters, sea urchins multiply → they eat kelp → kelp forests collapse → all kelp-dependent species decline. One species affects the whole system!

exercises.question: Why do SALMON swim UPSTREAM to spawn (lay eggs)?
choices: they prefer cold water at all times
upstream freshwater habitats provide safer, oxygenated, gravel-bedded spawning grounds where young salmon can develop away from ocean predators
exercises.exp: Salmon return to their birthplace using smell and magnetic navigation. Cold, clear, gravel-bedded streams provide ideal conditions for egg development and juvenile growth.

exercises.question: MIMICRY in animals means ___.
choices: one species evolving to resemble another for survival advantage (e.g., harmless species copying a poisonous one)
the genetic copying of traits between species
exercises.exp: Mimicry: harmless hoverflies mimic black/yellow wasp colours — predators avoid them thinking they sting. Batesian mimicry exploits a real species' reputation!

exercises.question: Which group of vertebrates has SCALES and BREATHES THROUGH GILLS its WHOLE LIFE?
exercises.exp: Fish have scales and gills throughout their lives (unlike amphibians that switch from gills to lungs). Fish are entirely aquatic vertebrates.

exercises.question: What is TERRITORIAL BEHAVIOUR in animals?
choices: the tendency to migrate long distances
defending a defined area against intruders of the same or other species to secure resources (food, mates, nesting sites)
following other animals to find food
exercises.exp: Territorial animals defend their space — through displays, scent marking, songs, or combat. Resources within the territory (food, mates) are the prize!

exercises.question: The HEART of a mammal has four chambers. What do the two VENTRICLES do?
choices: pump blood OUT of the heart — left ventricle to body, right ventricle to lungs
exercises.exp: Ventricles pump blood out: right ventricle → lungs (for oxygen); left ventricle → body (delivering oxygen). Atria receive returning blood.

exercises.question: Why do SOCIAL INSECTS (like bees) live in colonies?
choices: they cannot survive alone — they have no individual survival instincts
division of labour increases efficiency — queens reproduce, workers forage/build/defend — the colony achieves more than individuals could
bees are afraid of being alone
exercises.exp: In social insect colonies, specialised castes divide tasks. This efficiency allowed bees, ants, and termites to become among the most successful animals on Earth!

exercises.question: A CHORDATE is an animal that has (or had at some point) a ___.
choices: notochord (a flexible rod) — vertebrates are chordates with the notochord replaced by a backbone
exercises.exp: All vertebrates are chordates — they all had a notochord at some stage of development. In vertebrates, it is replaced by the vertebral column.

exercises.question: Why are apex PREDATORS important to ecosystem health?
choices: they are the most numerous animals
by controlling prey populations, they prevent overgrazing and maintain biodiversity — the 'trophic cascade' effect
they are the most colourful animals
they recycle nutrients by eating decomposers
exercises.exp: Remove apex predators and prey populations explode → overgrazing → habitat degradation → biodiversity loss. Wolves reintroduced to Yellowstone transformed the whole ecosystem!
